Consult Summary:
- 32-year-old woman with 7 days of fever, alternating hot/cold episodes, night sweats, myalgias, nausea, and fatigue after rural travel in Vietnam 4 weeks ago; acute undifferentiated febrile illness with malaria high on differential. Urgent in-person evaluation and labs arranged.

History:
- Presenting complaint/timeline: Fevers for ~7 days; alternating hot/cold with night sweats; generally unwell.
- Associated symptoms: Diffuse myalgias, nausea, poor appetite, low fluid intake, fatigue. OTC ibuprofen/paracetamol give partial, temporary relief.
- Pertinent negatives: No cough, sore throat, ear pain, diarrhea, neck stiffness, new/worsening headache, rash, joint swelling/tenderness, dysuria, urinary frequency.
- Past medical history: Chronic posture-related back pain (in physiotherapy). Baseline headaches related to screen use/weather; migraine history unclear (see conflicts).
- Medications: Paroxetine (Seroxat). OTC paracetamol and ibuprofen as per recommended doses during this illness. Took daily malaria prophylaxis during Vietnam trip (drug unspecified).
- Allergies: Seasonal/pollen (hay fever). No medication allergies reported.
- Family history: Father died of myocardial infarction at 68.
- Social/preventive: Nurse; up to date on vaccinations including Hepatitis B. Non-smoker. Moderate alcohol. Regular moderate exercise. Recent travel: multi-week trip across Vietnam including rural countryside/trekking/cycling and cities; returned 4 weeks ago.

Examination:
- Teleconsultation only; no vitals or physical exam documented.
- No labs or imaging performed yet.

Impression:
- Acute undifferentiated febrile illness post-travel.
- Leading considerations (from transcript and consistent with DDx):
  - Malaria (likely): Rural Vietnam travel; paroxysmal fevers with chills/sweats, myalgias, nausea; prophylaxis not fully protective. Planned thick/thin blood films.
  - Enteric fever (typhoid/paratyphoid): SE Asia travel, persistent fever with few localizing features; GI symptoms minimal.
  - Common viral syndrome (e.g., influenza/COVID-19): Fever and myalgias without focal bacterial source; occupational exposure as nurse, though lack of respiratory symptoms and night sweats make this less typical.

Plan:
- Urgent in-person evaluation today at clinic in central London for full examination.
- Laboratory tests after exam per clinician judgment; requested:
  - Thick and thin blood films for malaria.
  - Inflammatory markers and general blood tests.
- If clinic attendance is inconvenient, attend local A&E; clinician will document thought process and test requests in notes for reference.
- Administrative: Doctor to message admin to book urgent clinic slot; patient to call provided number to confirm appointment.
- Work status: Advised not to work until evaluation completed and cause clarified.
- Follow-up: Based on in-person findings and initial labs; urgency to be determined after examination.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements:
  - Vitals and full physical examination.
  - Specific lab panel details beyond malaria films/inflammatory markers.
  - Pregnancy status.
  - COVID-19/respiratory viral testing status.
  - Clear hydration/dietary guidance and safety-netting (e.g., when to seek urgent care if worsening).
● Conflicts between transcript and DDx:
  - Headache/migraine history: patient states “No migraines” initially but later notes sometimes struggling with migraines—conflict noted.
● Transcript quality:
  - Teleconsultation without examination; some pauses/clarifications; otherwise coherent history.
